{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-ct-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"e1ee52444aa2cef11814ef493efa4bf9cacb39bb1b17ea7ef9a2464fcfac6eb8","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-ct-class-d:lineage:10","source_registry_sha256":"07bbe76598f0084cdb2ee450c7050097675dacd13ccc4c40045c307297557e80","source_liveness_sha256":"8fea57e2daef73f0a94408791d2027c4fc2c9799e8d48060efecbf84d96aedf5"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Before you drive: vehicle, belts, phones, insurance","heading":"C — Before you drive: vehicle, belts, phones, insurance","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Before you drive: vehicle, belts, phones, insurance

FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A13
Only the brakes stop the car, so noise, odd smells, a floor bound pedal or pulling aside all send the car to a mechanic. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]
FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A13
Signals, brake, tail and head lights must all work as seen from outside, and a skewed headlight that blinds others needs fixing. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]
FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A13
Strip snow, ice and frost from every window, keep wipers and washer fluid ready, clean glass inside too, and replace cracked windshields. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]
FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A13
Bald tires stretch stops and fight turns on wet roads, so check pressure against the manual or door jamb monthly and before long trips. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]
FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A13
The penny test parks Lincoln head first in the tread groove: covered crown means safe rubber, bare head means replace. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]
FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A13
A failed emissions check grants sixty days to repair and retest the vehicle. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]
FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A13
Drivers owe their cars the owner manual maintenance schedule, since neglected cars strand and crash their owners. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]
FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A14
Repeated bouncing or wrestling the wheel after bumps points at worn shocks and a mechanic visit. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]
FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A14
Leaky exhaust can kill riders swiftly, so never idle in a shut garage, crack a window during long idles, and test the system on schedule. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]
FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A14
A sick engine may fade, stall, drink fuel and foul air, even dying mid road, so keep its manual service dates. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]
FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A14
Fuel burning feeds climate change with carbon dioxide, which buyers fight by shopping emissions and economy ratings and by driving thriftily. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]
FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A14
Steering that fights back or answers late belongs in a mechanic bay before the next drive. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]
FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A14
The horn serves only as a warning to others, though that warning can save a life. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]
FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A14
Connecticut orders belts on every occupant plus proper child restraints before rolling, and airbags never excuse bare belts against side, rear or rollover hits. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]
FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A14
Set seat and mirrors before moving: rearview frames the back glass, side mirrors the flanks, confirmed by leaning forward to glimpse the car side. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]
FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A14
Stow loose cargo and clear the floors so nothing flies in a stop or wedges beneath the brake pedal. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]
FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A14
Aftermarket tint and lighting swaps can break legal equipment standards. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]
FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A14
An unbelted driver and an unbelted rider each draw their own citation and a seventy five dollar fine. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]
FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A14
Two part belts demand both lap and shoulder straps, and auto shoulder belts still need the manual lap buckle against sliding out. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]
FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A14
Babies under two or under thirty pounds ride rear facing with a five point harness, and tots of two to five or under forty pounds ride rear or forward facing still harnessed. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]
FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A14
Kids of five to eight or forty to sixty pounds use a harness or booster, older bigger kids a booster or belt, age weight ties break toward stricter seats, and rear facing seats never face a live front airbag. [A14]
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]
FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A15
Every driver must see seven to sixteen year old riders belted, every occupant must wear one, and each bare rider earns a citation. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]
FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A15
Belts release in under a second, fire and sinking traps are rare, and a belted rider stays conscious to escape. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]
FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A15
More than half of road deaths strike within twenty five miles of home, many on streets posted below forty five miles per hour. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]
FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A15
Staying belted inside beats ejection into traffic, and side struck riders slide toward the impact rather than away. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]
FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A15
A twenty five mile per hour head on hit matches a full speed bicycle into a wall or a three story sidewalk dive, far past bracing. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]
FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A15
Handheld phones and mobile devices stay off on public highways even in traffic stops, parked shoulders allow use, adults may go hands free only, and sixteen and seventeen year olds may use nothing at all. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]
FACT_ID: sec03-F28 | anchor: A15
Any age driver may call out emergencies to responders, hospitals, clinics and police or fire outfits, and adult peace, fire and ambulance crews may use handhelds on duty. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]
FACT_ID: sec03-F29 | anchor: A15
A teen phone ticket counts as a moving violation, convicts under eighteen into a license suspension, and feeds the retraining tally. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]
FACT_ID: sec03-F30 | anchor: A15
Registered cars need unbroken insurance, lapses draw a DMV warning offering a compliance pact and fine, silence suspends the registration, and bare registration bans the road. [A15]
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]
